Turning Moo into Moolah Livestock Wealth

By: Diana Lucas | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Summary:
I like to do things where people say you’re crazy it will never work. ”

In 2015 Ntuthuko Shezi, using R300.00 from a panel beating business he had sold, bought 26 cows to start Livestock Wealth. The idea: crowd farming, putting investors and aspirant farmers together. Investors either buy a cow or a share in a cow. They get a return on their money when the farmer sell’s the cow or calves for a profit.

“It's a stock exchange environment where the farm is the company, the cows are the stock and the babies are the dividends. This form of "crowd farming" is an alternative option aimed at both African and international investors who can't relate to "imaginary things" like unit trusts, a cow, on the other hand, is a very real asset. Before there was money, cows were the currency, and cows are still a currency in most parts of Africa."

Today, 2019 the company has livestock across South Africa worth R40 million and 1000 investors…which with a finance deal with Rand Merchant Bank he expects to grow to 10 000 investors by 2020.


Further information:
Ntuthuko grew up in rural Ndwedwe in KwaZulu-Natal, with a single mother, a teacher who sold sweets, fish and vetkoek for extra money at the school she worked at. His grandparents embedded agriculture in the family economy, they kept cows for milk but every year when Shezi’s mother was at teachers training school and they needed to pay the fees, they sold a cow which paid for the year.

Ntuthuko believes the success of his venture is due in large part because it speaks to the heritage of African people: cattle. It is a new investment opportunity for the South African market – where you invest your money in cows rather than unit trust and shares.

A potential investor can invest in three different types of cows, an easy cow, a free range cow or a pregnant cow.
With an Easy Cow there is a six month investment R580 at which stage it goes to an approved abattoir who pay a market related price according to weight. The interest is divided between investors, farmers and Livestock Wealth.
Free Range Cow – An investor invests in its own cow with a price tag od around R11 000. Six months later when the cow is sold the investors get back their original investment with a return of 4-7%.
With a pregnant cow its all about the calves that are born.
Dividends are linked to the weight of the cow
“The first two things people want to know is: What happens if my cow dies, and is Livestock Wealth legitimate?”
The answer to the first question is Cow owners are cushioned against the risk that comes with owning cattle (death, theft disease) because of insurance the farmers take out.
To answer the second question, Shezi says investors receive a tax invoice for each cow and relevant papers. An ownership certificate is issued by the company. 
“If something happens to me or my business, the investor can come and take his cow,” he says.

Investors receive a ‘My Farmbook App’, an app for them to keep track of their cow. It’s health, weight, progress. This high tech but traditionally inspired app offers people with no access to land, time and skills the opportunity to own livestock in a professionally managed farming operation.

Last year Shezi signed a deal with Woolworths supplying them with free range beef with cows sourced from their farmers. Since April last year 64 tons of beef have been supplied -passing Woolworths strict protocol to ensure their standards were met.

Like Shezi’s grandparents, many South Africans own cattle but are not seeing significant returns,
Wandile Sihlobo, chief economist of the Agricultural Chamber of South Africa, says that livestock are an important component of the agricultural sector making up 51% of the sectors gross value in South Africa BUT this 51% has decreased in the last few years. In 2013, South African’s had 13.7 million herd of cattle in 2018 this number had fallen to 12.8 million. This means that for people like Shezi, they have a valuable contribution as they are increasing herds. Furthermore, 40% of the Livestock Wealth cattle belong to small black farmers in the Eastern Cape and Kwa Zulu Natal this is a great platform to link them to the market.

Livestock Wealth is the perfect entry point for the rural economy to get into the formal market, cash economy enables people to invest in a cow.

Shezi has gone further and turned his attention to fresh produce, his new idea is Connected Gardens’ This allows people to grow beetroot, cabbages, lettuces etc in wooden planters Investors buy a planter for R 8 200.00 and earn a rental paid by farmers over a period of a year. This covers the cost of seeds and equipment.
“ We are hoping this will be a game changer in lowering the barrier to entry for millions of aspirant farmers.”
People who have had no opportunity to become part of a supply chain to a large retailer, hospital or restaurant/chain, now can farm small crops and ‘ Connected Garden’ will use the mass harvest to leverage the buying.
Planters come equipped with camera and sensors so Livestock Wealth can monitoe the progress of the planters.

Press Release:


From Moo to Moolah – the Livestock Wealth App
In a world of volatile financial markets and abstract investment products, electro-mechanical engineer Ntuthuko Shezi’s smartphone application links investors to the ancient practice of cattle farming – and high yields as the beef price steadily increases. His app has enabled suburban urbanites to own livestock in successful farms, while assisting farmers to access capital for their operations. Now a multi-million Rand undertaking, KwaZulu-Natal born Shezi is expanding his partnerships and products to include macadamia nut cultivation and vegetable gardens. Carte Blanche meets the inventor and his investors who are seeing their dreams yield fruit.
Producer: Diana Lucas | Presenter: Claire Mawisa


Script:


Fancy owning, a cow, a herd of cows or even a percentage of a cow, well that was the brainwave of management consultant Ntuthuko Shezi,

Shezi: We are like this UBER company we match the farmer who has the cows with this investor who wants to own the cow.
.
V/O
Shezi’s company, Livestock Wealth, enables anyone to invest in cows. The cows are cared for on a farm, you reap the rewards when your cow gives birth or is sold as beef. All this can be done at the click of a smartphone.

Link : A crazy idea, linking Africa’s oldest source of wealth – cows with modernity, the stock exchange and in effect allowing aspirant farmers to invest in cows.

Ntuthuko Shezi,
CEO of Livestock Wealth

Claire: Was it easy to share this idea and concept with others?
Shezi: For the longest of time I only told a few people cause I didn’t want people to think I had grown crazy in fact our big break came in 2014 There is this event called the SAB social innovation awards, having drinks says so thid there is the CEO of the innovation hub go tell him about this thing of yours and I go and say to him I have this thing about people owning cattle as an investment and he connected to me like that,

V/O
And just two years later Shezi won SAB’s social Innovation award.

Link It’s the African practice your cattle as your wealth Ntuthuko understood this because his grandmother would sell a cow to pay for his mother’s education so he grew up understanding the connection between agriculture and the economy.

Shezi: So I was born in Twetwe and the economy there was agriculture. So at home they had cattle it wasn’t a lot 5/6 cows but they used those cows to pay for everything that needs to be paid for. There were no loans from the banks at the time, but they were wealthy they had cattle that bred and multiplied and grew in value

Wandile Sihlobo
Chief Economist: Agbiz
Wandile:I think agriculture is a hot topic in South Africa today because it helps us address some of the challenges that we are facing .We sit now as a country where we are experiencing low growth and also high unemployment and also there are higher poverty rates.

V/O
Agricultural economist Wandile Sihlobo heads up business research at the Agricultural Business Chamber (Agbiz).

Wandile: The livestock sector in South Africa is really the key contributor when you look at the agricultural economy. About 48 % of the value of the agricultural economy is the Livestock sector. We have about 12.8 million head of cattle so value terms it is good but I think the other thing that is important right now is just the prices of beef starting to gain a bit of momentum supported by what’s happening globally and that is going to benefit some of the guys that are in the beef market at this point.

V/O
Challenge No 1 was finding the right farmers, who knew what they were doing, Bill Van Lelyveld , has a farm near Vryheid, he was the first to come on board.

Bill Van Lelyveld
Bill: I was very impressed the way he presented it, the idea was so innovative and my reaction was well what are we waiting for, lets do it.

V/O
There are three ways to invest. You buy a pregnant cow, when the calf is six months old, its sold and you get the profit, which works out to around 13 %.

V/O
Or you invest in a Free Range cow in the last 6 months of it’s life, getting a profit of around 6.5 % for the six months.

V/O
And if you don’t have a lot of cash, there’s the stokvel style where a few people can invest in a cow ….sharing the dividends when the cow is sold.

V/O
The plus for the farmer is he’s getting capital to sustain his running costs, in the period where there is no no profit from the cow.

Shezi: So if farmer has 100 cows he can say I have 10 investable cows out of my 100 which I will sell to my investors through your platform and then he can realize lets 10 000 a cow so 100 000 rand income the farmer now has which he can use to invest in the rest of his cows. LW has evolve into a bank for farmers to access funds from the crowd which is people like you and me,

V/O
Nontokozo Sabela was one of the first investors in 2016 she bought a pregnant cow for 18 000,

Nontokozo Sabela

Nontokoz: I bought the cow gave birth after 8 months then they buy it back.

V/O
A year later she bought another cow.

Nontokozi These are my babies
Claire: You wanted the convenience of having a cow but not managing it?
Nontokozo: Ya,I don’t want to know when it’s pregnant I don’t want to know when its sick I’ve got to do vaccination.

V/O
Every cow has a unique ID, with its vital statistics, and while you’re sitting in Johannesburg…you are forever linked to your cow through the app.

Nontokozo We have a farm book so on that farm book they update whatever’s happening so now there is drought drought…..don’t worry feed load keep updating us.

Shezi : So really the terminology which is the app is this bridge between the technology that is the farm where the cow is and the investor is 1000 miles away. we are going further as well the electronic tracking of livestock.

V/O
Just like a fitbit, the cow will wear a collar which tracks it’s steps, it’s weight, it’s whereabouts.

V/O
Livestock Wealth have partnered with 12 farms around the country, Calvin Ngema is the farm manager on Bill’s farm.

Calvin Ngema
Farm Manager
They are well taken care of and how do we know is that every year the cows give birth and only a productive cow gives birth and well maintained

Claire: What’s in store for the future do you want to have more cows?
Nontokozu: Yes I want to have five.
Claire; Do the dividends come at the right time?
Nontokozo: Yes they come at the right time yes.

Shesi : So we are better than the banks, if you go to any of the banks today you will be lucky if you get 7% but we are coming in between 10 – 14% depending on how the beef price performs.

Wandile: On the demand side it looks positive that globally beef is starting to recover SA is participating on a global beef market. but, the risk is to say with the climate change story and then if they get a lot of drought that could be worrying they need to be thinking about and how they hedge themselves.///

Claire: How relevant today if people are talking about block Chains and the stock exchange and bitcoins?
Shezi: It is absolutely relevant you know President Trump tweets something cow is still growing its eating grass and its increasing in value and it’s totally unhinged from whatever political uncertainty doesn’t if JZ President or Ramaphosa or which faction is in power/the cow grows in value and will be meat which costs more than last month.

Claire: What if a rock falls from the sky hits the cow on the head and it dies?
Shezi: So if the cow, the farmer replaces it, that is part of the agreement with the farmer, so your investment is 100% safe.

Link The company started with 26 pregnant to the value of 250 000 rand with only 14 investors now they have 2000 investors owning cows to the value of 50 million rand.

Shezi: We have dreams of seeing Livestock Wealth being not only listed on the JSE but also in NY stock exchange. !5% of our investors our outside the SA, who never set foot in the country but they are like I want to put my money in a cow… Some people have copied us which is great, if people are copying it means we are doing something right.

With an Easy Cow there is a six month investment R580 at which stage it goes to an approved abattoir who pay a market related price according to weight. The interest is divided between investors, farmers and Livestock Wealth. Free Range Cow – An investor invests in its own cow with a price tag od around R11 000. Six months later when the cow is sold the investors get back their original investment with a return of 4-7%. With a pregnant cow its all about the calves that are born. Dividends are linked to the weight of the cow “The first two things people want to know is: What happens if my cow dies, and is Livestock Wealth legitimate?” The answer to the first question is Cow owners are cushioned against the risk that comes with owning cattle (death, theft disease) because of insurance the farmers take out. To answer the second question, Shezi says investors receive a tax invoice for each cow and relevant papers. An ownership certificate is issued by the company. “If something happens to me or my business, the investor can come and take his cow,” he says. Investors receive a ‘My Farmbook App’, an app for them to keep track of their cow. It’s health, weight, progress. This high tech but traditionally inspired app offers people with no access to land, time and skills the opportunity to own livestock in a professionally managed farming operation. Last year Shezi signed a deal with Woolworths supplying them with free range beef with cows sourced from their farmers. Since April last year 64 tons of beef have been supplied -passing Woolworths strict protocol to ensure their standards were met. Like Shezi’s grandparents, many South Africans own cattle but are not seeing significant returns, Wandile Sihlobo, chief economist of the Agricultural Chamber of South Africa, says that livestock are an important component of the agricultural sector making up 51% of the sectors gross value in South Africa BUT this 51% has decreased in the last few years. In 2013, South African’s had 13.7 million herd of cattle in 2018 this number had fallen to 12.8 million. This means that for people like Shezi, they have a valuable contribution as they are increasing herds. Furthermore, 40% of the Livestock Wealth cattle belong to small black farmers in the Eastern Cape and Kwa Zulu Natal this is a great platform to link them to the market. Livestock Wealth is the perfect entry point for the rural economy to get into the formal market, cash economy enables people to invest in a cow. Shezi has gone further and turned his attention to fresh produce, his new idea is Connected Gardens’ This allows people to grow beetroot, cabbages, lettuces etc in wooden planters Investors buy a planter for R 8 200.00 and earn a rental paid by farmers over a period of a year. This covers the cost of seeds and equipment. “ We are hoping this will be a game changer in lowering the barrier to entry for millions of aspirant farmers.” People who have had no opportunity to become part of a supply chain to a large retailer, hospital or restaurant/chain, now can farm small crops and ‘ Connected Garden’ will use the mass harvest to leverage the buying. Planters come equipped with camera and sensors so Livestock Wealth can monitoe the progress of the planters.
